_comment: Triage of the corpus's guard failures (RFC 0035, section 11; RFC 0038, section 5), checked by
scripts/corpus-gate.py. `guardFailures` lists the reports of a test suite that the gate does
not count as traps: {config, file, line, verdict, note, kind (optional, a run-time report
kind), rfc}. The verdict is "project-bug" for a true bug of the project, its note the
evidence (an ASan run, a reduced program, the source), or "accepted" for a false trap an
Accepted RFC accepts, which `rfc` names ("0037"). Any other false trap is a bug in WeaveC
and is never triaged. An entry no run names is reported as stale without failing.

guardFailures.note: RFC 0038, the programs tier: faulthandler._read_null reads through a null pointer on purpose (x = NULL; y = *x), for test_faulthandler, which checks that the process dies of it.

RFC 0038, the programs tier: _PyInterpreterState_GET reads tstate->interp with no thread state when a fatal error test (Py_FatalError without the GIL) reaches _PyFaulthandler_Fini; the reference build dies of the same SIGSEGV there (a macOS crash report of the reference run on darwin-arm64: _PyInterpreterState_GET, get_state, _PyObject_Free, _PyFaulthandler_Fini, fatal_error).

RFC 0040 section 0: a race at shutdown in CPython 3.13's drop_gil (Python/ceval_gil.c), which reads tstate->eval_breaker (FORCE_SWITCHING, _Py_eval_breaker_bit_is_set) after drop_gil_impl has unlocked the GIL's mutex; the comment there names the race (python/cpython issue 104341). Reproduced on linux-aarch64 under load (-j8 on three CPUs) with RFC 0040's stacks: a daemon thread in os.write -> PyEval_SaveThread -> drop_gil read 8 bytes at offset 24 of its own PyThreadState (336 bytes, allocated by alloc_threadstate in ThreadHandle_start), which the main thread had freed in _Py_Finalize -> _PyThreadState_DeleteList after SystemExit, in the window between the unlock and the read. It does not reproduce with each test file alone or at -j4 on four CPUs; an ASan run would need the same timing and was not made.

RFC 0038, the programs tier: fsmonitor_publish reads state->current_token_data->batch_head while the daemon's token data is null (an FSEvents callback during shutdown); the reference build's daemon dies of the same SIGSEGV in fsmonitor_publish (a macOS crash report of the reference run on darwin-arm64), which the tests tolerate.

RFC 0038, the programs tier: gnulib's rawmemchr (coreutils 9.5) reads the string a word at a time, past the byte it stops at and so past the end of its object; AddressSanitizer stops the same reads (help-version, shuf, csplit, tty-eof).

RFC 0038: the TLS test helper (tests/src/test_helpers/ssl_helpers.c at c765c831) passes the EC client certificate's DER buffer with mbedtls_test_cli_crt_ec_len, the length of its PEM form, so mbedtls_x509_crt_parse reads buf[buflen - 1] 722 bytes past the DER array, in the next global. ASan, which leaves no redzone between those globals, passes all 886 tests of the suite.

RFC 0039, the programs tier: kwsys's testProcess test 3 writes through a null pointer on purpose (*invalidAddress = 0, 'Provoke deliberate crash'), for kwsys.testProcess-3, which checks that the parent sees its child die of it.

RFC 0039, section 7: test/ostream-test.cc's write_to_ostream_max_size hands fmt::detail::write_buffer a buffer whose data is a null pointer and whose size is SIZE_MAX, so write_buffer calls std::ostream::write(nullptr, PTRDIFF_MAX). write obtains its characters from the array s points to ([ostream.unformatted]), which here is none; the test passes with the reference compiler and ASan only because its mock streambuf overrides xsputn and reads nothing.
